title.narrative: UNESCO: Our Rights, Our Lives, Our Future Zambia
UNESCO: Our Rights, Our Lives, Our Future Zambia

description.narrative:
Målet för projektet Our Rights, Our Lives, Our Future Zambia (O3 Zambia) är att uppnå förbättrade resultat inom sexuell och reproduktiv hälsa samt utbildning för ungdomar genom att förebygga hiv, minska antalet tidiga och oönskade graviditeter samt att eliminera könsbaserat våld.
Insatsen syftar till att stödja sexualundervisning i skolor inom ramen för läroplanen. Sexualundervisning är en läroplanbaserad process för undervisning med fokus på de kognitiva, sociala, emotionella och fysiska aspekterna av sexualiteten för att utrusta ungdomar med kunskaper, färdigheter, attityder och värderingar som gör det möjligt för dem att förstå hur deras val påverkar det egna och andras välbefinnande; hur de utvecklar respektfulla sociala och sexuella förhållanden och förstår sina rättigheter och kan säkerställa att dessa skyddas. Sexualundervisningen handlar även om att få ungdomar att inse vikten av hälsa, välbefinnande och värdighet.
Projektets huvudsakliga mål är följande:
1. Att öka ungdomars, både pojkars och flickors, tillgång till sexualundervisning av hög kvalitet som behandlar ämnen som HIV, könsbaserat våld, förebyggande av tidiga och oönskade graviditeter och barnäktenskap. 2. Att skapa säkrare, hälsosammare och inkluderande skol- och närmiljöer som är fria från könsbaserat våld, mobbning och diskriminering. 3. Att stödja förebyggande och hantering av tidiga och oönskade graviditeter. 4. Att säkra och stödja samhällsstöd för sexualundervisning och sexuell och reproduktiv hälsa och rättigheter (SRHR) och främja större engagemang av män och pojkar. 5. Att utöka kunskaps- och bevisbasen för sexualundervisning för dess planering och genomförande.
Den huvudsakliga målgruppen är ungdomar i skolan från årskurs 5 till 12 (cirka 10–19 år). UNESCO strävar efter att nå minst 2 miljoner elever i årskurs 5–12. Sekundära målgrupper omfattar 90 000 lärare i tjänst, 15 000 lärarstudenter och 9 600 rektorer. Projektet förväntas också nå 4 250 000 personer (föräldrar, vårdnadshavare, religiösa ledare, ungdomar som av olika anledningar inte går i skolan) genom massmedia och olika plattformar på sociala medier. Projektet kommer att vara landsomfattande men genomföras med mer riktade aktiviteter i fokusprovinserna Central, Eastern, North-Western, Lusaka och Southern. De flesta av dessa provinser har ett högt antal tonårsgraviditeter, skolavhopp och barnäktenskap. Lusaka väljs ut på grund av ett högt antal HIV-drabbade och ett högt antal könssjukdomar bland ungdomar samt att huvudstaden spelar en ledande roll i genomförandet av projektet kring sexualundervisning.

The Project goal of the Our Rights, Our Lives, Our Future Zambia project is that Adolescents and young people in Zambia attain improved sexual and reproductive health and education outcomes through sustained declines in new HIV infections, early and unintended pregnancy, and gender-based violence. Underpinning the intervention is the provision of comprehensive sexuality Education (CSE) in schools within the school curriculum. CSE is a curriculum-based process of teaching and learning cognitive, social, emotional and physical aspects of sexuality in order to equip adolescents with Knowledge, Skills, Attitudes & Values enabling them to consider how their choices affect their own well-being and that of others; develop respectful social & sexual relationship; Understand and ensure the protection of their rights throughout their lives; and ultimately realize health, well-being & dignity.
The main objectives of the project are as follows;
1. To increase adolescent boys’ and girls’ access to good quality CSE programmes that integrate content on HIV, Gender Based Violence (GBV), prevention of Early and Unplanned Pregnancies (EUPs) and child marriage. 2. To create safer, healthier, and inclusive school and community environments that are free from GBV, bullying, and discrimination. 3. To support the prevention and management of EUPs. 4. To secure and sustain community support for CSE and Sexual Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR) services and promote greater engagement of men and boys. 5. To expand knowledge and evidence base on CSE for planning and implementation.
The main target population are in-school adolescents from grades 5 through 12 (approximately 10-19 years old). UNESCO aims to reach at least 2 million learners in grade 5-12; Secondary targets groups include 90,000 in-service teachers; 15,000 Pre- service teachers and 9,600 head teachers. The project is also expected to reach 4,250,000 people (parents, guardians, religious leaders, young people out of school) through mass and social media platforms. The project will be implemented countrywide but with more intensive activities in focus provinces Central, Eastern, North-Western, Lusaka, and Southern provinces. Most of these have high rates of teen pregnancies, school drop outs and child marriage. While Lusaka is chosen due to high rates of HIV and STIs among young people and its capacity to play a lead role in CSE implementation

sector.narrative: Ending violence against women and girls

description.narrative:
The programme has performed well during the period. Below some examples of results against the 2024 targets:
Throughout the duration of the project, UNESCO delivered a highly relevant programme to improve sexual and reproductive health and education outcomes for adolescents and young people in Zambia.
The project exceeded in the following targets:
1) Number of grades 5-12 learners reached by high quality sexuality education curricula that is evidence based and age appropriate;
2) Number of pre-service teachers trained in CSE; and
3) Number of community members sensitized on the re-entry policy through mass media. The target for the number of Grades 5-12 learners reached by high quality sexuality education curricula that is evidence based and age appropriate went over the expected 2 million. Number of pre-service teachers trained in CSE had a target of 15,000 where the result at the end of 2023 was 17,316. For the number of community members sensitized on the re-entry policy through mass media, the target was 4 250 000 and ended up being over 6,5 million people throughout the 5 focus provinces in Zambia.
Despite these successes, the implementation during the COVID-19 pandemic led to restrictions which limited both project activities and the delivery of CSE content in schools. The project was therefore reprogrammed and adapted during the second year to ensure continuation of activities, using alternative tools such as virtual platforms, television broadcasts, and radio programmes.
Furthermore, organized conservative opposition to CSE led to resistance from parents as well as other community members and even discomfort among teachers in delivering CSE content. The response to this focused on reshaping the narrative around CSE by organizing awareness campaigns and community dialogues to spread accurate information about SRH and maintain engagement in the project.
Additionally, UNESCO mobilized its partners and key stakeholders to adress the opposition through deepened advocacy efforts within communities. This led to increased engagement and strategic collaboration with members of parliament as well as ministries of education. A notable example of this collaboration was in November 2023, when the Speaker of the National Assembly launched the Advocacy Strategy on Adolescent and Reproductive Health, guiding members of parliament in advancing the implementation of Life Skill Health Education (LSHE) in Zambia.
Although many parents and community leaders were opposed to the delivery of CSE, due to a lack of understanding, positive attitudes towards CSE were observed among learners who expressed a need for certain critical topics to be further elaborated on. The project contributed to improved outcomes in sexual and reproductive health, gender, and education for adolescents and young people at both community and national levels. At the community level, teachers and pre-service teachers were trained to deliver quality, age-appropriate CSE, and CSE books were distributed to learners and educators across the five focus provinces. At the national level, the project successfully mobilized political stakeholders to commit to advancing adolescent sexual and reproductive health and rights.
